1.10.10 Land Acknowledgement. “The University of Rhode Island occupies the traditional stomping ground of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People. We honor and respect the enduring and continuing relationship between the Indigenous peoples and this land by teaching and learning more about their history and present-day communities, and by becoming stewards of the land we, now too, inhabit.” #22-23-2

1.10.20 Background. The University of Rhode Island, the state’s land and sea grant research institution began as the state of Rhode Island’s Agricultural Experiment Station and agricultural school chartered in 1888. In 1892, the institution’s name was changed to the Rhode Island College of Agriculture and the Mechanic Arts. This name was subsequently changed to Rhode Island State College in 1909. The current name- the University of Rhode Island— was adopted in 1951 by an act of the State of Rhode Island’s General Assembly. For a complete history of the University, refer to https://www.uri.edu/about/history/.

1.10.30 Mission. The University of Rhode Island is the state’s flagship land and sea grant research institution, with a commitment to urban initiatives. A student-centered research institution, URI actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to advance knowledge and to develop informed residents and leaders. URI is committed to high-quality education, community engagement, and solving the world’s most important challenges. Situated on the traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People, URI strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers, learners, and community members.
1.10.40 Values. The University of Rhode Island is committed to the following foundational values:
* Freedom to learn, teach, create, and conduct research with integrity in the pursuit and dissemination of new knowledge aimed at contributing to the public good.
* An inclusive, accessible, equitable and diverse community whereby we respect the rights and dignity of all.
* Intellectual curiosity, lifelong learning, leadership, and scholarship in creating a thriving URI community in service to Rhode Island and the world.

The prevention sciences graduate certificate combines skills with methods to understand how to reduce risk and promote health and healthy development.
There is an emphasis on examining social determinants of health with the aim of enhancing equity and decreasing disparities.
Additionally, this program provides intellectual development and training to a diverse community of students who can benefit from foundational and applied skills in health promotion and disease prevention but require flexible academic pathways (Strategic priority 2; Goal 1; Action 1).
This certificate can be completed to meet requirements in the Master's of Professional Studies program and the Master's of Public Administration program.
For the Master's of Professional Studies (30 credits total), students complete two certificates, and six additional credits of coursework.
The Prevention Science certificate can be included as one of the certificates toward completion of the degree.
For the Master's of Public Administration (36 credits total), students complete three certificates to complete the degree.

The Prevention Science certificate can be included as the third certificate the students complete towards their degree.
The certificate could also be taken as a stand-alone certificate for any interested students.
One of the key elements of prevention science is the partnership with key community stakeholders (both public and private) who can work together to develop and implement appropriate interventions that address today’s health-related challenges.
Using evidence-based practices, applied learning, and real-world scenarios, students will be able to explore a range of issues through the lens of promoting and protecting health (e.g., social justice, family trauma, substance abuse and/or other addictions).
Therefore, the interdisciplinary nature of the program aims to foster meaningful interactions amongst students who bring expertise from a variety of health backgrounds.

This program aligns with the URI strategic plan priorities and goals in several ways to include: 1) Strategic Priority 1 (Broaden Our Impact), Goal 1: Contribute to broad and deep impacts on the social, cultural, and economic ecosystems across Rhode Island, the nation, and beyond. 2) Strategic Priority 2 (Enhance Student Achievement), Goal 2: Increase graduate student enrollment and degree completion. 3) Strategic Priority 4 (Power the University of the Future), Goal 4: Expand research and new academic programs and services through an increased focus on revenue generation.
Offered completely online and asynchronously, this program targets working professionals across a myriad of health sectors who wish to advance within the workforce while still holding full-time jobs.
This will be attractive to students while meeting employers’ needs.
Additionally, the stackable design of this program highlights the intersection of specialties that employers look for while offering a flexible path for students.
Furthermore, the appeal of the in-state competitive tuition speaks to the accessibility of the program nationwide and beyond.

We currently offer a Developmental Science Master's program as a traditional face-to-face graduate program.
We are proposing this graduate certificate in Prevention Science to offer a new pathway for working professionals and other individuals seeking an online Master's degree focused on health sciences and health prevention.
The Developmental Science Master’s degree program will pause enrollment for the 2023/2024 academic year until we decide the future of the program.
One of the primary drivers for our decisions regarding the future of the Developmental Science program’s future will be based on the PhD in Health Sciences Program and its possible plan to add a Master’s degree pathway for PhD students.
